name: Historical workforce estimates are not credible current totals

attribution.legal_posture: Official OHCHR reporting on overseas-worker deployments and the absence of a credible current total; historical estimates remain historical

caveats: Historical figures, enforcement totals, vendor observations, incident counts, and application counts remain separate measures; a current workforce total requires a defined common denominator.
Some deployments report student cover; this fact supplies context rather than a screening heuristic for students, remote workers, or nationals of any country.

statements: A/HRC/60/58 reports that overseas workers in information technology, construction and hospitality continued to be deployed after the Security Council repatriation deadline, reportedly under student cover in some cases.
OHCHR expressly states that no credible current figure is available for the total number of DPRK overseas workers remaining abroad.
Historical workforce estimates, incident counts and application volumes therefore must not be combined or relabeled as a current worldwide worker total.

sources.support: Supports continued overseas information-technology deployments reportedly using student cover in some cases and OHCHR's express statement that no credible current overseas-worker total is available
